text:
Emma: noticing spike in 502/504s for hosted inference in eu1 this morning, started ~07:35 UTC. Several customer escalations, e.g. #CS-9271 and #CS-9273. Error surface: gateway timeouts + upstream reset. Logs show 'upstream prematurely closed connection' and 'connection reset by peer'.

Michael: are we seeing this cross-AZ only or entire region?

Emma: mostly between edge-pop eu1-edge-3 -> backend eu1-ml-cluster (across AZs). CPU/GPU look fine, no capacity alarms. Net metrics show increase in retransmits and RTT spikes on host gateways.

Karen: I'm on it, pulling flows. Can you paste a sample request id?

Emma: request_id=8f2d9a3c from ticket CS-9271. Timestamp 07:37:12.

Li: customer repro steps: repeatable via SDK generate requests, ~30% of requests return 502s, with longer tails on latency (p95 -> 1.6s -> 3.2s). They reported this started after a maintenance window by a carrier? Not sure.

Michael: we see BGP path churn out of transit provider AS64511 around 07:30-07:40 UTC. Peers show aspaths changing and a new longer path with multiple extra hops. Suspect transient blackholing or MTU mismatch on new path.

Raj: runtime reports upstream errors like `kv_cache_miss`? or `upstream_reset` more often?

Emma: mostly upstream_reset/timeouts. No model-side OOMs. Gateway shows tcp_close with RST.

Karen: running mtr from eu1-edge-3 to one of the inference nodes (10.12.45.23):

```
mtr -r -c 8 10.12.45.23
Start: Tue Mar 15 07:45:01 2026
HOST: eu1-edge-3                             Loss%   Snt   Last   Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
  1.|-- 10.254.0.1                              0.0%     8    0.4   0.5   0.3   1.1   0.3
  2.|-- 203.0.113.5                             0.0%     8    0.9   1.1   0.8   1.8   0.3
  3.|-- 198.51.100.29                          12.5%     8    5.2   6.6   5.1  12.9   2.9
  4.|-- 198.51.100.33                          25.0%     8    8.7  10.3   8.6  16.4   2.9
  5.|-- 10.12.45.23                             0.0%     8    9.1  10.1   9.0  14.0   1.9
```

Karen: intermediate hops 3-4 show loss; looks like provider-side issue.

Michael: that lines up with the transit provider BGP logs — AS64511 withdrew preferred path and chose a path via partner AS33445 which prepended AS path, causing fragmentation in some carriers. There were also MTU-discovery ICMPs being dropped.

Raj: runtime: if TCP-level fragmentation or ICMP PMTUD failures occur, connections can stall when MSS > path MTU. Our HTTP clients don't fallback fast. Could result in upstream resets when proxies can't deliver payload.

Emma: any quick mitigations? Customers need stability.

Karen: short-term: 1) fail traffic away from the affected transit at edge-router via policy (we can pin to provider B until they fix). 2) apply MSS clamp on gateway nodes to 1420 to avoid PMTUD reliance. 3) increase gateway connection retries/backoff.

Michael: Provider claims they rolled a config change. Reverting to the previous best path should fix link. I'm opening a ticket with them and requesting immediate rollback.

ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026-321: "eu1 transit provider AS64511 path change -> increased packet loss -> hosted inference 502s". Severity: P1. Pager notified.

Li: letting affected customers know: posting interim notice in CS tickets, recommending retry/backoff on client. Asking if we can provide a temporary region failover for large accounts.

Raj: added a runtime guard to treat upstream_reset as transient and retry idempotent generation calls up to 2x with jitter. Pushing patch to edge config (no model restart).

Karen: applied MSS clamping on eu1-gateway-az-a and az-b at 08:05 UTC: `sudo iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1420`. Monitoring now.

Emma: initial metrics after changes: 502 rate down from 3.2% -> 0.6% over 15m. p99 latency improving. Customer CS-9271 confirmed fewer failures.

Michael: provider rolled back their path change at 08:18 UTC. BGP tables show stable aspath to eu1 via AS64511 primary.

Karen: postmortem tasks: - confirm no residual packet loss, run mtr across edge fleet, remove MSS clamp if unnecessary after validation, capture pcaps for later analysis.

Emma: notes for support playbook: if customers report sudden 5xx + edge retransmits, check transit BGP churn, mtr from edge to host, look for mid-path loss, consider temporary MSS clamp + provider failover + runtime retry.

Li: I'll consolidate customer-facing timeline and update CS tickets. Also offering larger customers region failover if they'd like.

Raj: rolling the runtime retry to eu2 and eu3 as precaution. Will monitor for any negative impact (duplicate completions). We only retry idempotent calls.

Michael: provider said they will add monitoring on their partner peering and avoid path prepending during maintenance windows. Also asked for BGP community tagging for faster diagnosis.

Emma: closing the live incident in 1h. Will open postmortem doc with timeline and RCA draft. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

SupportBot: updated incident channel with ticket links: https://redwood.example/cases/CS-9271, https://redwood.example/incidents/INC-2026-321

Karen: follow-ups scheduled: capture MTRs from 5 edge nodes, run `tcptraceroute` to confirm MTU behaviour, and verify our HTTP clients degrade gracefully.

Emma: ok. I'll start the postmortem draft and include mitigation list and runbook updates.

Li: customers are stable and CS-9271 acknowledged update. Closing that ticket pending postmortem.

Emma: last check at 08:50 UTC shows steady state, watchers will keep an eye for 24h.

Karen: saving logs and pcaps to /var/incident/INC-2026-321/ for further analysis.

Emma: thanks all, great coordinated response.
